subject: Fallback drill + immutable pin strategy for private maintenance
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofía Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, ops@edgecloud.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fallback drill + immutable pin strategy for private maintenance

Team / EdgeCloud,

Quick note ahead of our scheduled maintenance window on Sep 3–4: we want to run a short fallback drill and validate the immutable pin (pinlock) shelving procedure for our Private customers. Goal is to prove we can:
- Shelve a pinned version out of traffic (immutable pin -> shelved state)
- Evacuate a canary fleet and failover to the fallback model variant without downtime to control-plane requests
- Run the rollback path (unshelve -> resume) end-to-end with telemetry validation

I attached a condensed runbook and a checklist (immutable_pin_runbook_v1.pdf, fallback-drill-checklist.xlsx). Ask list:
1) EdgeCloud: can you confirm a 2-hour dry-run window on Sep 2 at 02:00–04:00 UTC where we can exercise network cordon + routing failover?
2) Ops: who will own the unshelve rollback step (Doc step 4.3)? We want a named owner for the run.
3) Infra: confirm that KV cache warmup is enabled for the fallback model so token-latency spike is controlled.

Proposed play: Karthik leads run coordination, Sofía runs comms and validation checks, Vanessa owns telemetry/alerts, Neha is rollback owner. EdgeCloud to provide a short-lived test token and a BGP/route change window.

Please reply with confirmations and any objections by EOD Aug 30 so we can lock the maintenance plan.

Thanks,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sofía Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fallback drill + immutable pin strategy for private maintenance

Karthik / Sofía,

Thanks for the heads-up. We can provision a 02:00–04:00 UTC dry-run on Sep 2 for the test token and controlled route change. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- During the shelve flow, the on-prem network agent will mark nodes as drained; we need a 15-minute draining window for graceful session teardown. Is that acceptable?
- For the unshelve rollback, our recommendation is to do an incremental un-shelve of 10% of capacity then 50% then 100% to avoid sudden KV cache spikes. Is the runbook flexible for that?

Owner names: I can assign our SR manager (Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@edgecloud.com>) to own the unshelve steps; he'll be on the call.

EdgeCloud also requests a copy of the test harness (or a small synthetic workload) to validate routing correctness during the drill — we can run it from our staging VPC.

— ops@edgecloud.com

On Mon, Aug 29, 2026 at 15:12, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / EdgeCloud,
> 
> Quick note ahead of our scheduled maintenance window on Sep 3–4: we want to run a short fallback drill and validate the immutable pin (pinlock) shelving procedure for our Private customers....
From: Sofía Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, ops@edgecloud.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fallback drill + immutable pin strategy for private maintenance

Thanks Miguel / EdgeCloud — that all sounds reasonable. Short notes / updates:

- Drain window: accept 15 minutes. We'll update the runbook step 3.2 to reflect graceful session drain and add a smoke-check step right after the 15-minute mark.
- Incremental unshelve: agreed — we'll run 10/50/100 increments and capture KV cache metrics at each stage. Vanessa, please define guard rails (acceptable token-latency delta and cache-miss thresholds).
- Run ownership: Neha confirmed rollback ownership, Miguel will be on the call as EdgeCloud's unshelve lead. Karthik will coordinate the overall timeline.
- Test harness: attaching a small synthetic harness (see attachment reference) and a short snippet of curl tests that EdgeCloud can run in staging. EdgeCloud, please run the harness during the 02:00 UTC slot and share logs to the Drive folder in the related_links.

Action items for next 48h:
- Vanessa: telemetry thresholds and dashboard URL (OPS-4821)
- Neha: draft the rollback checklist and validate permissions for unshelve API (Doc step 4.1)
- Karthik: update runbook with incremental unshelve and drain time notes; send final comms to customers on Sep 1 morning

I updated the runbook link in the Drive and attached the lightweight harness to this thread. If there are no objections, I'll lock the dry-run and the Sep 3–4 maintenance window later today.

Sofía
--
Sofía Ivanova
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
